summary: Run 2 of M1-S03, built to the remedy-B amendment that unblocked run 1's template-provenance refusal. Twelve Apex files at apiVersion 67.0: two after-update triggers, two handlers, a service, a Queueable, a Finalizer, three test classes (19 test methods), and verbatim copies of the two self-contained templates the step still cites. The escalating transaction publishes Tier2_Escalation__e and enqueues exactly one Queueable for the whole transaction; the Queueable runs every callout before any DML, classifies 429/502/503/504 and connection failures as transient and 400/401/403/404/422 as permanent, and throws before writing anything when a transient failure still has attempt budget so Tier2WebhookFinalizer owns the retry with an AsyncOptions MinimumQueueableDelayInMinutes back-off. The queue is resolved by DeveloperName through a per-transaction cache with no Id literal anywhere, tests included. All three declared checkers exit 0 with zero findings, every -meta.xml parses at 67.0, and brace/paren/bracket/string balance was verified mechanically on all twelve files. Five undeclared artefacts (the two template copies with their meta XML, and this step's deploy-order.md). No compile check ran: build_mode is design-only and there is no offline Apex compiler in the sf CLI.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per GATES.md Gate D row 3: Gate B resolved every symbol, but no target_org_alias exists in a design-only build so Gate C's compile check did not run at all and coverage is unknown. The envelope says that plainly rather than implying the code was checked. Two UNVERIFIED items also remain open (the event's Severity__c mapping, and the Case_Link__c URL form), both flagged at the line and in deploy-order.md section 5.

findings.title: The org loses its trigger kill switch and its data-load bypass
findings.detail: Remedy B dropped templates/apex/TriggerHandler.cls because its closure needs TriggerControl and Trigger_Setting__mdt, which no step ships. TriggerControl is what lets an admin deactivate a handler from Setup without a deployment, and what honours the TriggerControl_BypassAll Custom Permission during a data load. Neither exists here. A bulk load that reassigns Case ownership into Tier_2_Engineering will escalate every affected Case, with no bypass; switching the feature off is a deployment of CaseTrigger.trigger-meta.xml with status Inactive. The per-transaction recursion guard is not a substitute - it stops this handler re-entering itself inside one transaction and does nothing about a load, which is many transactions each doing what it was asked.

evidence.missing_metadata: Trigger_Setting__mdt (templates/apex/cmdt/Trigger_Setting__mdt/) is shipped by no step of this plan

findings.recommendation: Add the Apex-foundations step standards/build-orchestration.md section 4's Apex row note prescribes - a metadata-builder step shipping Trigger_Setting__mdt (and, if the logger is wanted back, Application_Log__c and Logger_Setting__mdt) - then let this step extend TriggerHandler as intended. Decide it at the M1 gate rather than after a data load discovers it.

findings.title: Tier2_Escalation__e.Severity__c is mapped from Case.Priority and nothing in the plan says it should be
findings.detail: The event carries a Severity__c Text(40) and no clarification maps it to a Case field. Case.Priority is the only severity-shaped field this build has seen, so it is what the service writes. Q11's answer speaks of 'a Severity 1 escalation', which is not the shape of standard Case.Priority values (High / Medium / Low), so the org may carry a severity field this build never saw. A wrong value here is silently wrong on the ops dashboard rather than loud.

findings.title: The transient-retry branch and the chained tail are deliberately uncovered
findings.detail: A transient failure with attempt budget left makes execute() throw so the Finalizer owns the retry; an unhandled exception in a job run by Test.stopTest() fails the test method, so the throw-to-Finalizer path is not asserted. Only one job may be added to the queue from a test context, so chainRemainder() is guarded by Test.isRunningTest() and the chained tail is not driven either. Both ends of the behaviour are asserted by other means: the classification directly, and the exhausted-budget outcome through a real job.

process_observations.observation: The two templates that survived remedy B are the two that are self-contained - neither MockHttpResponseGenerator nor TestDataFactory references another templates/apex class or names a custom object - which is the same property that would have let the other three survive if the build shipped their metadata.
Every declared checker passed on the first run of the emitted package, with zero findings at any severity rather than zero blocking findings - so nothing was left standing as an accepted warning.

Two library checkers disagree with a library skill about where Test.setMock goes: skills/apex/apex-named-credentials-patterns/references/code-examples.md section 6 puts setMock before Test.startTest, while check_callouts_and_http_integrations.py flags exactly that as HIGH and quotes the guide line requiring startTest first - which is the ordering skills/apex/test-class-standards/references/code-examples.md uses.

The step's own acceptance-test description for the callouts checker states that the checker fails on 'a test with setMock after startTest', which is the opposite of what the code does - it fails when no startTest precedes the first setMock. The prose would mislead anyone fixing a failure by reading the plan instead of the checker.

Nothing in the 45 clarifications says whether the org already has an after-update trigger on Case; this step ships CaseTrigger and a second trigger of the same name will not deploy, while two triggers on one object is a consolidation problem rather than a deploy one.
An existing Case trigger would make this a consolidation rather than an addition.
